    <input id="mul_a" width_description="">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
    <input id="mul_b" width_description="">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
    <output id="mul_en_out" width_description="">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
    <output id="mul_out" width_description="">Product output signal with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
  </ports>
  <logic_description>
    <description>
            Notice that below descriptions are along with tags  <logic />. These tags  <logic /> could be described more detail in the below description in the  <implementation /> tag.
            With a  <logic type="combinational_logic" />, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this  <logic type="combinational_logic" /> can be declared as a `reg` but only be used in always(*) block.
            With a  <logic type="sequential_logic" />, must construct this logic as `reg` declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other  <logic type="sequential_logic" /> or  <logic type="combinational_logic" /> states.
            With a  <logic type="sequential_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just place this operation sequence in below mentioned description.
            With a  <logic type="combinational_logic_operation" />, no declaration for this keyword. Just based on the keyword `assign` to construct description of this combinational logic operation.
            With a  <logic id="temp" /> tag with width_description and depth_description attributes declaration, such as  <logic id="temp" width_description="[a:b]" depth_description="[c:d]"/>, it must be declared as `wire [a:b] temp [c:d]` if its type is a `combinational_logic`. Otherwise, the logic must be declared as `reg [a:b] temp [c:d]` if its type is a `sequential_logic` or a `combinational_logic` driven in a `alway @(*)` block.
        </description>
    <logic id="mul_a_reg" width_description="" depth_description="" type="sequential_logic">
        8-bit sequential logic.
        If  <input refid="rst_n" /> is deactive,  <logic refid="mul_a_reg" /> is reset to 0.
        Otherwise,  <logic refid="mul_a_reg" /> is set to  <input refid="mul_a" /> if  <input refid="mul_en_in" /> is active, else  <logic refid="mul_a_reg" /> is set to 0.
        </logic>
    <logic id="mul_b_reg" width_description="" depth_description="" type="sequential_logic">
        8-bit sequential logic.
        If  <input refid="rst_n" /> is deactive,  <logic refid="mul_b_reg" /> is reset to 0.
        Otherwise,  <logic refid="mul_b_reg" /> is set to  <input refid="mul_b" /> if  <input refid="mul_en_in" /> is active, else  <logic refid="mul_a_reg" /> is set to 0.
        </logic>
    <logic id="temp" width_description="[15:0]" depth_description="[7:0]" type="combinational_logic">
         <logic refid="temp" /> is a logic with 16-bit width and 8-bit depth, `[15:0] temp [7:0]`.
        `temp[0]` is set to value of shift-left-0 of `mul_a_reg` if `mul_b_reg[0]` is active.
        `temp[1]` is set to value of shift-left-1 of `mul_a_reg` if `mul_b_reg[1]` is active.

  <implementation>The module utilizes a pipeline architecture to improve performance. It consists of several key components:
Input Control:
The module includes an input enable signal, mul_en_in, which controls the multiplication operation.

Input Registers:
The module includes registers, mul_a_reg and mul_b_reg, to store the input multiplicand and multiplier, respectively.
On the positive edge of the clock signal, the module samples the input values and stores them in the corresponding registers.
The registers are only updated when the input enable signal is active.

Partial Product Generation:
The module generates partial products by performing bitwise operations between the multiplicand and the individual bits of the multiplier.

Final Product Calculation:
The module sums up all the partial sums to obtain the final product.
It uses a register, mul_out_reg, to store the accumulated sum.
On the positive edge of the clock signal, the register is updated with the sum of all partial sums.

Output Assignment:
The module assigns the output product value, mul_out, based on the output enable signal and the value in mul_out_reg.
If the output enable signal is active, indicating a valid product, the value in mul_out_reg is assigned to mul_out.

</implementation>
